integrity: Uses exact combinatorial counting, classical Pieri and Kostka positivity, and an existing published Stirling-transform identity. Finite verification is supportive and does not constitute an infinite proof or independent validation.
scientific_limitations: The strict statement compares exponent profiles at fixed total prime-factor multiplicity; it makes no magnitude comparison between integers.
The number of parts and the ordered-factorization length must both lie between two and the total exponent sum.
The extremal integer is not unique when its prime bases are varied; uniqueness concerns exponent multisets.
Earlier implicit symmetric-function treatments may contain an equivalent statement.
title: Strict prime-exponent majorization for ordered factorizations and sum systems
